ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a parallelogram tilted to the right, and a broken-line-shaped internal boundary extends from the upper-left vertex to the lower-right vertex, dividing the parallelogram into two parts. The region labeled P1 is on the lower left, and the region labeled P2 is on the upper right. Reasoning: Let the length of this common broken-line boundary be C. Let the lengths of the upper and lower sides of the parallelogram be a, and the lengths of the left and right slanted sides be b. The perimeter of P1 consists of the common broken line C, the left slanted side b, and the lower side a, so Per(P1)=C+b+a. The perimeter of P2 consists of the common broken line C, the upper side a, and the right slanted side b, so Per(P2)=C+a+b. Because these two expressions are the same, the perimeters of P1 and P2 are always equal.

raw_record.question_text: A parallelogram is divided into two parts, $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$, as shown in the picture. What is always true about the perimeters of $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$?

method.method_draft: Describe the image first: the parallelogram is split by a jagged interior line running from the upper-left vertex to the lower-right vertex; P1 is the lower-left piece and P2 is the upper-right piece. Let the length of the jagged dividing line be C. Let the parallelogram side lengths be a for the top and bottom sides and b for the left and right slanted sides. From the image, the perimeter of P1 consists of the common jagged line plus the left side plus the bottom side, so Per(P1)=C+b+a. The perimeter of P2 consists of the same jagged line plus the top side plus the right side, so Per(P2)=C+a+b. Therefore the two perimeters are equal.

method.method_draft: Describe the image first: the split line is irregular, but it is shared exactly by both P1 and P2, and it connects two opposite vertices of the parallelogram. Ignore the shared jagged line temporarily, since it will be counted once in each perimeter. Now compare only the two outer boundary routes between those same endpoints: P1 uses the route along the left side and bottom side, while P2 uses the route along the top side and right side. In a parallelogram, a half-turn about the center maps the top side to the bottom side and the right side to the left side, preserving lengths. Thus the two outer boundary routes have equal total length. Adding back the same shared jagged divider to both gives equal perimeters.
